events.title: Publication of The Communist Manifesto
events.description: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels' pamphlet The Communist Manifesto was first published in London by the Communist League, outlining a theory of class struggle and a critique of capitalism.
events.significance: The Manifesto became one of the most influential political documents in history, shaping socialist and communist movements and political thought worldwide for more than a century.

events.title: Assassination of Malcolm X
events.description: Civil rights leader Malcolm X was shot and killed while about to deliver a speech at the Audubon Ballroom in Harlem, New York City. He was 39 years old, and three men were later convicted of the murder.
events.significance: His death cut short the career of one of the most influential figures in the African American civil rights and Black nationalism movements; his posthumously published Autobiography of Malcolm X became a landmark of American literature.

events.title: Nixon Arrives in China
events.description: U.S. President Richard Nixon arrived in Beijing for a week-long visit and met with Chairman Mao Zedong, becoming the first U.S. president to visit the People's Republic of China.
events.significance: The visit ended more than two decades of diplomatic isolation between the two nations and began the process of normalizing relations, reshaping Cold War geopolitics.

events.title: First Telephone Directory Issued
events.description: The first telephone directory was issued in New Haven, Connecticut, by the District Telephone Company. It was a single page listing 50 subscribers.
events.significance: It marked the early growth of telephone communication as a public utility and the beginning of a publishing format that would be used by millions for over a century.

events.title: The New Yorker Publishes Its First Issue
events.description: The first issue of The New Yorker magazine, founded by Harold Ross and his wife Jane Grant, went on sale in New York City.
events.significance: The magazine grew into one of the most prestigious publications in the United States, known for its journalism, fiction, cartoons, and criticism.
